title: Computational cognitive modeling
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn to turn theories of the mind into models that make quantitative predictions, and to fit and compare them, in Python: why model cognition, signal detection and choice models, the drift-diffusion model of decisions, reinforcement learning models of choice, Bayesian models of perception and cognition, models of categorization, memory models, connectionist models and their history, maximum likelihood fitting, model comparison with likelihoods and information criteria, and parameter recovery.
primary_reading: Probabilistic Models of Cognition by Goodman and Tenenbaum (free online)

weeks.1: Why model cognition? Marr's levels and model types
weeks.4: Signal detection and choice models revisited
weeks.8: Model comparison: likelihood ratios and information criteria
weeks.9: Bayesian models of perception and cognition
weeks.12: Parameter recovery, model recovery and good practice

blocks.deliverable: Write the likelihood of supplied choices under a simple model.
Fit a model to supplied choices by a grid search.
Simulate a diffusion model with supplied noise and compare its predictions.
Week 7 midterm; compare two learning models on supplied data.
Build a Bayesian model of a concept-learning task.
Run a parameter-recovery study for a fitted model.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Model-fitting study: fit two competing cognitive models (for example a delta-rule learner and a Bayesian learner, or two decision models) to a supplied behavioral data set in plain Python, compare them with likelihoods and an information criterion, run a parameter and model recovery check, and write a short paper on what the comparison shows and what it cannot.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
